q: I dropped the idea that if she was comfortable with it, I would love to be in the room (I’m a nurse, I’ve seen multiple births, I can be so supportive for her).
cx: A nurse whose best friend is being induced in two days has been invited into the delivery room.

q: She’s allowed 3 people in the room. Her mom, her husband, and they all agreed I should be the third.
cx: Who the friend chose for her three birth-room places.

q: I’m glad to be there as someone who can hopefully talk her through all the medical jargon
cx: What the nurse-friend hopes to offer during the induction.

q: How screwed am I besides my future sleep having 2 kids under 13 months.
cx: A father still on paternity leave learns his wife is pregnant again; the baby is due in June.

q: I go into work 2or3 days a week to stretch my leave out further.
cx: How he spreads 10 weeks of paid state leave.

q: I don’t want to feel like every family visit means I have to hand my baby over, wake him up, rearrange his naps, or make sure everyone gets their “turn.” Sometimes I just want to sit with my baby and be his mom
cx: A mother of a three-month-old on in-laws expecting constant access since the birth.

q: She’ll say things like, “Ugh, but don’t you need a break?” or “I feel bad that you can’t even drink your coffee.”
cx: Her sister-in-law's lines when not handed the baby.

q: she literally said to me, “I heard you don’t like letting people hold your baby.” 😭
cx: A relative repeats family gossip about her boundaries.

q: I’m perfectly happy to have a village that supports me and respects my boundaries. I’m not interested in a village where I have to make my baby available to everyone so nobody gets offended.
cx: Her definition of a helpful village after the birth.

q: Taxis for example regularly take a couple of hours to turn up, if they turn up at all. Ambulances coming up to birth had a call out time of 7 or 8 hours and obviously they’re really not designed to take people to hospital when in labour.
cx: Four months on, a rural UK mother explains why no transport led her to an elective c-section.
r: IVF, c-section, birth trauma and perinatal mental health care

q: I will always regret that I didn’t give birth to my baby “naturally”. I feel I was robbed of that experience.
cx: Same mother on the birth she did not have.
r: IVF, c-section, birth trauma and perinatal mental health care

q: He gives me a break for example so I can eat, he’ll hold the baby, but hand baby back literally before I’ve swallowed the last mouthful, before I’ve even put my cutlery down.
cx: How her partner's help looks with a baby who wants only her.
r: IVF, c-section, birth trauma and perinatal mental health care

q: He’s saved nothing for when my maternity pay runs out in December and I’m probably going to have to go back to work and leave baby with him and it makes me sick to my stomach.
cx: Her worry about maternity pay ending.
r: IVF, c-section, birth trauma and perinatal mental health care

q: What things and actions would you have loved to receive when pregnant, but also after giving birth and learning how to care for your new child?
cx: A friend of a woman due in spring asks mothers what help they wanted.

q: I will go there and buy all the groceries and cook in their home, and of course clean everything up afterwards. As long as she permits, of course. :)
cx: Her plan, since freezer meals cannot travel the distance.

q: I genuinely felt like every time someone came into our bedroom or knocked asking about the baby just to take him from my arms, I lost confidence in myself as a mother.
cx: A 24-year-old first-time mother two weeks postpartum, living with her in-laws.

q: I’m staying at my mother’s house now and I have had such a peaceful morning with my son. No one knocking on my door, no one telling me to hand him over, no one running to the room because he’s crying. Just peace.
cx: After moving out of her in-laws' house in the first week.

q: I’m all for someone trying to be helpful but I don’t need help right now and I will ask when I do.
cx: What she wants her mother-in-law to understand.

q: She texted me and said I got her going home outfit! Well shouldn’t that be my decision?
cx: Her mother is buying most baby clothes and nursery items without asking her.

q: I’m not sure if I want her in the delivery room and I know that would crush her.
cx: She wants the birth to be hers and her husband's.

q: Acted SHOCKED when I told her that I wanted an epidural, and told me to think about it before I commit such a mistake
cx: Living abroad, she lists her mother-in-law's comments during a hard pregnancy.
r: ER visits, medication, perinatal depression and hospitalisation

q: how she absolutely had zero symptoms during her pregnancies and how she did everything by herself and never experienced any pain and climbed Mount Everest 2 days PP. (Not really but yk what I mean lol)
cx: Her mother-in-law's own pregnancy story, told while she was exhausted.
r: ER visits, medication, perinatal depression and hospitalisation

q: I live in a foreign country with no one that I know and no support system, I’ll go through PP only with my husband who can only take 2 weeks off from work.
cx: Her picture of the postpartum weeks.
r: perinatal depression and hospitalisation in same passage

q: “when the baby is 4 months old, I’ll take her to give you a break, I would have loved to take her earlier than that but you wouldn’t let me”
cx: One of her mother-in-law's offers of help.
r: ER visits, medication, perinatal depression and hospitalisation
